correctness.rationale: The regular polygon is the intersection of halfplanes tangent at radius r; along any ray the radial boundary equals r/cos(alpha-delta) where delta is distance to the nearest vertex. The union inherits the nearest-vertex formula. The angles covered at radius t are equal-radius neighborhoods of repeated vertex phases, with total measure n sum_j min(g_j,2eta(t)). Sum of truncations is bounded by min(sum_j g_j,m c), and a nonuniform gap vector has a strict deficit at c=average, hence on an open set of levels. Polar integration gives the exact area, and the largest gap gives the centered inradius. Taylor's theorem gives disk-deficit coefficient pi^2 R^2 tan(pi/n)/n. 240 coordinate-built polygon unions had maximum area error 1.78e-15 and perimeter error 7.11e-15; 15 sampled circle-cover checks differed by at most 0.00139 radians, and four asymptotic tests passed. The proof is analytic; finite experiments cannot establish the universal claim.

originality.rationale: The 2014 primary full text fixes and studies equal-spaced common-center constructions and proves only a perimeter/area ratio for them; the all-radius angular-coverage majorization and its rigidity are mathematically stronger in a different direction and are not derived by that statement. Broader union papers concern perimeter/area ratios or translated pieces, with no verified implication covering every radius. The 2015 rotation-intersection question concerns facet counts of intersections, not unions. Public mathematical-record searches found no implication-equivalent theorem. Remaining risks from unindexed sources and partially accessible earlier literature are recorded rather than treated as proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: Sharp coverage at each concentric radius is a natural exact geometry invariant relevant to finite rotational coverage of a disk. The same equally spaced configuration stochastically dominates every other orientation's radial reach and is uniquely optimal for every strictly positive radial mass, area and maximal centered contained disk. The result provides exact complete extremal classifications for all n,m and the sharp 1/m circumdisk coverage deficit, going materially beyond known fixed perimeter-area quotient calculations. No arbitrary numerical slice is singled out and no downstream theorem is required to motivate the all-parameter optimization.
